intended_codes.status: unwitnessed operators: frozen post-hoc after run 1 (703cdde1), unchanged since catalogue version 2; witnessed operators (family H, catalogue version 3): written after the verifier's tier V3 existed, intended codes frozen post-hoc from the codes it emits; not held-out
intended_codes.basis: catalogue version 2 drops intended-code names that do not exist in the verifier and adds the codes the verifier emits for the damage, chosen after run 1 and the V3a follow-up were read. Catalogue version 3 adds family H operators written from the ODES design and contracts and the control plane's witness producer code, without reading the verifier's damage tests; their intended codes are the verifier's V3 codes named in its docs/tiers.md and the ODES report contract's family H table
intended_codes.primary_figure: any_code detection; localized (intended-code) figures are secondary

revises.note: catalogue version 3.3 adds nine unwitnessed operators over the evidence check hardening of verifier 31708c33 (attempt identity and lifecycle, acknowledgement freshness and receipt comparison, tenant on one side only; a tenth, a refusal recorded before its evaluation pass, was tried and not catalogued because the native refusal rows carry no evaluation time) and changes no earlier operator id, function, mutant or intended code. Version 3.2 (set as of qualification 52a20fa3) revised version 3.1 (qualification f1592c37, digest sha256:4ae13f234ac214a02d34d247d8b7f9a086cbf8f18156aaf166acf164b4d42a62): it reclassified H4.destination-row-dropped-uncorroborated as a known-limit control (expected outcome accept, labelled post-hoc: the witness profile does not cover destination.json, ODES decision 30-A, ODES #89). Version 3.1 (H8.witness-file-absent as an input-error control) revised version 3 (qualification ce684ec6, digest sha256:86e4b43449acdf7976aaf3d091d33c2d5b4636f5e64fe3a4d22c4d8f23b9d00c, the set run 4 measured)

supersedes.note: catalogue version 3 keeps the 81 unwitnessed operators of version 2 unchanged (same functions, same intended codes) and adds the witnessed operators

operators.description: A second, different closing row appended to an attempt that an acknowledged or partial row already closed (not a repeated record).
A later row of an attempt names another decision than the attempt's first row.
A later row of an attempt names another effect than the attempt's first row (an attempt is fixed to its first row's identity).
An attempt row written against a held decision.
An ``attempted`` row appended to an attempt that an acknowledged, partial or failed row already closed.
The ``attempted`` start row of an attempt removed.
A second attempt lifecycle started for an effect that already has one.
An ``attempted`` row appended to an attempt that stands at ``unknown`` (an uncertain attempt may only be followed by a closing row).
A closeout that names an observation time no accepted observation has.
The closeouts of uncertain attempts removed.
A binding's ``amount`` written ``50.00``, ``5e1`` or ``50.0e0`` for ``50.0``: one float, one canonical byte string under the pinned profile (post-hoc, was W3).
All insignificant whitespace removed.
Four-space indentation with CRLF line ends (valid JSON whitespace).
Every object's members written in a different order (the pinned profile sorts keys, so the content is the same).
A ledger row's ``amount`` written in a float spelling the pinned profile maps to the same bytes (post-hoc, was W3).
The proposal export's ``amount`` written in a float spelling the pinned profile maps to the same bytes (post-hoc, was W3).

A resolution check's id changed. Resolution-check ids and journal-check ids are separate producer ids and a completed journal check binds to a resolution check by stage, inputs and reasons, so the record stays consistent (post-hoc, was J2.completed-matches-no-resolution-check).
Some letters and digits inside string values written as ``\uXXXX`` escapes (same strings, other text).
A held decision whose ``result`` is flipped to authorized while its reasons stay.
An authorized decision that carries reasons.
An authorized decision with its binding removed (``null``).
The grant input's observed status contradicts its expected status under an authorized result.
The policy input's observed version contradicts its expected version under an authorized result.
A held decision whose reason is not in the pinned reason registry.
A journal-mode decision with its reason vocabulary version removed.
The grant input observed as ``revoked`` while the decision stays authorized (the one recomputable reason code).
The proposal amount changed and every commitment that depends on it recomputed (proposal, effect id, rows, ledger): self-consistent, so expected accepted.
The ``effect_id`` replaced consistently in every row and in the ledger: only the recomputed identity can show it.
A decision's ``effect_id`` replaced by another digest (rows that name the effect keep the original).
A ``tenant_id`` added to one decision's binding while the proposal carries none (a tenant on one side only is a difference, never a pass).
The proposal export's ``amount`` changed while the record's binding is not.
The proposal export's ``payload`` changed while the record's binding and payload commitment are not.
The proposal export's ``target`` changed while the record's binding is not.
A decision's operation horizon commits to a different proposal.
One resolution input's ``record_commitment`` altered in the decision (the resolution check keeps the original).
An input marked ``missing`` that still carries a record commitment.
The manifest file edited while the digests that commit to it are not.
A binding's ``manifest_digest`` replaced.
A binding's ``payload_commitment`` replaced.
A check's ``opened`` journal event removed.
A check's ``opened`` journal event written twice.
Two resolution checks listed in the reverse of their order.
A check left opened-only (its ``completed`` event removed) while its resolution check stays.
A completed check's journal event rewritten as ``interrupted`` while its resolution check stays (the inverse of the design's rewrite: no real clean trace holds an interrupted check).
A ledger effect row for an effect no decision names (an injected unauthorized effect).
A ledger effect row for an effect whose decision is a hold.
The amount inside an acknowledgement's effect receipt changed, so it differs from the ledger row.
A ledger row whose amount differs from the decision's binding.
A ledger row that names a different grant than the decision's binding.
A ledger row whose target differs from the decision's binding.
An acknowledgement that says ``duplicate: false`` and, in the same breath, ``newly_executed: false`` (the two flags claim the same thing).
An acknowledged attempt row written twice.
A second attempt (another attempt id, same effect) that also claims a fresh execution of the effect an acknowledged attempt already executed.
A second ledger row (under another key) for one effect, with the grant's effect count raised.
The ledger row of an acknowledged attempt removed (a dropped receipt).

The ledger row of an effect whose acknowledgement was lost removed, while the record holds an accepted applied observation of it (post-hoc, was R6: refusing is correct, the record contradicts the snapshot).

The ledger row of an effect whose acknowledgement was lost removed, with nothing in the record corroborating it (unknown attempt, no accepted applied or partial observation): the record does not say the row exists and the ledger has no sequence or chain, so expected accepted (post-hoc narrowing of the version 1 operator).
A member the contract does not declare, on an attempt row.
A member the contract does not declare, on a decision.
A member the contract does not declare, at the top level.
An attempt ``status`` outside the closed set.
A decision ``result`` outside the closed set (``deny``, ``safe_to_retry``, ``approved``).
A reconciliation ``result`` outside the closed set.
A required attempt member removed.
A required top-level collection removed.
A required decision member removed.
An ``extensions`` member whose name lacks the ``x-`` prefix.
An ``extensions`` member without the ``x-`` prefix on a decision.
A decision time written without a UTC offset.
An input time floor written without a UTC offset.
An observation (in every row that carries it) stamped after the evaluation time.
An observation (in every row that carries it) stamped long before the evaluation time.
A second ``effect_id`` member with a different digest written before the real one.
A second ``result`` member (the opposite value) written before the real one in a decision, so a last-wins parser reads the original.
A second top-level ``run_id`` member written first.
``NaN`` as a numeric value inside a declared ``x-`` extension.
A non-JSON constant as the proposal export's ``amount``.
A non-JSON constant as a decision binding's ``amount``.
A non-JSON constant as a destination ledger row's ``amount``.
A binding's ``amount`` written as an integer (``50`` for ``50.0``): a different canonical byte string, so a different number.
A ledger row's ``amount`` written as an integer.
The proposal export's ``amount`` written as an integer: its commitment no longer matches the record's.
One letter in a string of a decision binding replaced by the letter plus a combining accent (NFD form): different bytes, same look.
A lone UTF-16 surrogate escape inside a string in a declared ``x-`` extension.
A UTF-8 byte-order mark in front of the run record.
A very deeply nested array inside a declared ``x-`` extension.
A second JSON value after the run record.
A decision copied from another run in place of this run's decision.
The destination ledger of another run supplied with this run's record.
The proposal export of another run supplied with this run's record.

witnessed_operators.description: A whole float ``amount`` in a covered row written as ``50.00``, ``5e1`` or ``50.0e0`` (one float, one canonical form: the head is unchanged).
The holder inventory's members written in a different order.

A second holder with the id of an enumerated holder (kind ``other``). The profile defines no uniqueness rule; the ODES draft pins this as valid (``repeated-holder-id-is-not-refused``). Contract-valid, not value-equal: an accept is the contract's expectation.
All insignificant whitespace removed from the run record.
Every object's members in the run record written in a different order (the heads are over canonical rows, so unchanged).
An empty line before or between witness records (the producer's reader skips blank lines).
CRLF line ends in the witness file.
Letters of the run id written as ``\u00XX`` escapes (the same string).
Each witness line's members written in a different order (compact); same records.
The witness file without its final line end.
A further record over the unchanged record appended, correctly chained (a re-publication with nothing new: a valid witness).
Each witness line written with a space after every ``:`` and ``,`` (still one record per line).

The catalogue's self-consistent reseal (proposal amount changed, every dependent commitment recomputed) and the witness re-made over the resealed record with the same publication structure (each record's counts kept, heads and digests recomputed): the record and the witness rewritten together so that they agree.
A multi-record witness replaced by one fresh record over the current record (the witness's holder rewrote its history).

A fabricated intermediate publication inserted before the latest record: its counts lie between the previous record's and the latest's, its heads are right for those prefixes, and the chain is re-computed (the witness's holder added history that never happened).
One witness line written twice in a row (a duplicated digest line).
One record's ``digest`` replaced by another well-formed digest (not recomputed).
The first record given a ``previous_digest`` (it claims a predecessor the file does not hold), digest recomputed.
A forged record (a copy of an existing one, digest recomputed) inserted before the latest record without re-chaining what follows.
A held ledger head edited without recomputing the record's ``digest`` (the record no longer recomputes).
Two witness lines swapped (each record unchanged).
A later record's ``previous_digest`` pointed at another digest, the record's own ``digest`` recomputed (only the link is broken).
The whole chain re-chained with sequences starting at 1: links and digests consistent, sequence is not the index.
A record other than the latest removed from the chain, nothing re-chained (removing the latest is the H7 tail truncation).
One record's ``sequence`` no longer its index (shifted by 1 to 3), digest recomputed.
A record of another run's witness spliced onto this chain as its newest record, re-linked (sequence, previous digest, digest recomputed).
The run record's top-level ``run_id`` changed; the witness unchanged (the witness now covers another run than the record).
The run id upper-cased in every record, chain re-computed (a different string that reads alike).
The ASCII hyphen in the run id replaced by U+2010 HYPHEN in every record, chain re-computed (looks identical).
Every record's ``run_id`` replaced by another run id, chain re-computed (internally consistent, wrong run).
A trailing space appended to the run id in every record, chain re-computed.
The witness file of another run (whose records name a different ``run_id``) supplied with this run's record.
The witness file of another run that uses the same ``run_id`` string (the producers here name most runs ``run-1``): the run id cannot tell the runs apart, only the heads can.
A ledger entry whose ``count`` is 1 written as ``true``, digest recomputed (``True == 1`` in Python).
A ledger entry's ``count`` written as a float of the same value, digest recomputed.
A ledger entry's ``count`` written as a string, digest recomputed.
A ledger entry's ``count`` made negative, digest recomputed.
The ``digest`` member removed from one record.
An ``extensions`` object whose key has no ``x-`` prefix added to a record, digest recomputed.
A held head written in upper-case hex or without the ``sha256:`` prefix (not the digest form), digest recomputed.
An extra member (``algorithm`` or ``rows``) in a ledger entry, digest recomputed.
``count`` or ``head`` removed from a ledger entry, digest recomputed.
``ledgers`` written as a list of ``{name, count, head}`` objects instead of an object, digest recomputed.
One witness line written as a one-element JSON array holding the record.
One required member (``sequence``, ``previous_digest``, ``ledgers`` or ``run_id``) removed from a record, digest recomputed.
One record pretty-printed over several lines (the file is no longer one record per line).
``sequence`` 0 or 1 written as ``false`` or ``true``, digest recomputed (a Python bool compares equal to the integer).
``sequence`` written as a float of the same value (``1.0`` for ``1``), digest recomputed (equal in Python, not an integer).
``sequence`` written as a string (``"0"``), digest recomputed.
A member that looks like a signer, proof or publication time added to a record, digest recomputed (the profile has none; it must not be read as one).
``version`` of one record set to ``witness-digest/0.2``, digest recomputed.
``version`` of one record written as the number ``0.1``, digest recomputed.
``version`` of one record set to another profile's name (``holder-inventory/0.1``), digest recomputed.
``version`` with a trailing space, digest recomputed.
A UTF-8 byte-order mark in front of the witness file.
A second ``run_id`` (or ``ledgers``) member written before the real one in a witness line, so a last-wins reader sees the clean record.
An invalid UTF-8 byte inside the run id string of one witness line.
A lone UTF-16 surrogate escape appended to the run id string of one witness line.
A ledger entry's ``count`` written as ``NaN`` or ``Infinity``.
A second JSON value after the record on one witness line.
A random row of a fully covered run-record ledger removed; the witness unchanged.
The first row of a fully covered run-record ledger removed; the witness unchanged.
The last row of a fully covered run-record ledger removed; the witness unchanged.

Known-limit control (ODES decision 30-A, ODES #89): the destination ledger row of an effect nothing in the record corroborates (unknown attempt, no accepted applied or partial observation: the R6 shape) dropped in a witnessed trace. The witness profile covers the run record's list-valued members only; the destination snapshot is a different file, so the drop is as undetectable as without a witness. Expected outcome accept, labelled post-hoc; an accept is the measured limit, not a missed detection.
A covered ledger emptied (``[]``); the witness unchanged.
A covered ledger member removed from the record; the witness unchanged.

The record and the destination ledger replaced by their own earlier snapshot (taken at the first publication, a valid state of the same run), the full witness unchanged: a newer witness against an older record.
A row covered by an earlier record dropped and the witness's latest record re-made over the shrunk record (linked to the previous one): the earlier digest still covers the dropped row.
A covered row dropped and a new witness record made over the shrunk record appended, correctly linked (what ``publish_head`` refuses to do: laundering the drop into a fresh digest).
The latest record's count for a ledger raised by one (head kept), digest recomputed: the record now holds fewer rows than witnessed.
A whole-number float ``amount`` in a covered row written as an integer (a different canonical number); the witness unchanged.
A covered row dropped and a copy of the last row appended so the count holds; the witness unchanged.
An ``extensions`` member with one ``x-`` name added to a covered row (where the record's contracts admit extensions this is the one change only the witness can see); the witness unchanged.
A covered row replaced by a copy of another row of the same ledger (count unchanged); the witness unchanged.
One string value inside a covered row changed (a character appended); the witness unchanged.
Two distinct covered rows of one ledger swapped (count unchanged); the witness unchanged.
The latest record's count for a ledger lowered by one with the head kept, digest recomputed (the head no longer covers that prefix).
A held head replaced by another digest and the record's digest recomputed (a consistent witness holding a wrong head).
A holder's ``credential_ref`` written as a number or an object.
The inventory written as a one-element list holding the inventory object.
An ``extensions`` object whose key has no ``x-`` prefix, on the inventory or on a holder.
Where the record names the inventory: an extra holder added to the supplied inventory.
Where the record names the inventory: a holder removed from the supplied inventory.
Where the record names the inventory: a holder duplicated in the supplied inventory (so it is not the inventory the record names).
A holder id of 257 characters (the limit is 256).
An undeclared member (``revoked_at``, ``secret`` or ``state``) added to a holder.
``holders`` written as an object keyed by holder id instead of a list.
The ``holders`` member removed from the inventory.
An undeclared member (``signature``, ``complete`` or ``covers_classes``) added to the inventory.
A holder's ``kind`` capitalised (``Routed``).
A holder's ``kind`` set to a lifecycle word (``expired``, ``revoked`` or ``lapsed``) the closed set does not have.
A holder's ``kind`` removed.
``recorded_at`` a word, not a time.
``recorded_at`` without its UTC offset (a naive time) or as a bare date.
``inventory_id``, ``recorded_by`` or a holder's ``enforcement_point`` / ``holder_id`` set to the empty string.
``version`` written as the number ``0.1``.
``version`` set to another profile (``witness-digest/0.1``) or a next minor (``holder-inventory/0.2``).
A second ``kind`` member (``expired``) written before the real one in a holder, so a last-wins reader sees the clean inventory.
The latest record's count for one ledger lowered by one with the head recomputed over the shorter prefix, digest recomputed (consistent: the last row is now unwitnessed).
Every witness record re-made without one ledger and the chain re-computed (consistent; that ledger's rows are not covered at all).
The witness replaced by one record made over a prefix of one ledger (as if published before the later rows were appended); the record unchanged.

The latest witness record(s) removed so an older valid witness is replayed against the newer record: the remaining latest record covers fewer rows than the record holds (the rows appended since are unwitnessed, not damaged).
The witness file holding only line ends (no record; the producer's reader skips blank lines).
The witness file supplied empty (zero bytes).
``--witness`` names a path where no file exists: an input-error control (ODES decision 30-A), expected exit 2 and no report.
